The three pages are told apart by THICKNESS, not by collection, which is worth saying because their headings are identical.
pricing_note: A NEW GRAMMAR FOR THIS REGISTRY: THE CODE DOES NOT DETERMINE THE PRICE. One code spans FIVE finish groups and EIGHT depth bands - forty prices - and every other section held here so far has had the code decide, or a single price band decide. Here the finish group is an ORDER AXIS, which is exactly what domain rule 6 describes: per-order axes live outside the article code, like door version 78/75 and hinge side. So the group is NOT in the code and must be carried on the order line beside it. points_per_lm_by_group_and_band is deliberately named for both axes so nobody reads it as one.
depth_note: THE BAND IS CHOSEN, NOT DECODED. The printed depths are the TOP's own depth; our runs are 620 carcass, and the finished front is 644,5 (620 + 22 door + 2,5 front gap). CORRECTED 2026-08-29, and the correction is added rather than substituted (learned rule 9). THE SENTENCE THAT FOLLOWED HERE WAS WRONG: it said the bands "happen to sit 30 above the carcass depths this book sells (35->38, 62->65, 67->70), and that is an OBSERVATION, not a printed rule". IT IS A PRINTED RULE. The SAME BOOK prints it as a table 71 printed pages earlier - Volume 3 printed p.39-40, "Top depths" - with three variants and every one of our eight bands in it. The note was written from p.110, the PRICE page, and nothing had asked the rest of the book. See top_depth_rule below. What remains true: 650 is the band this kitchen orders, 380 serves the 350-deep units, and a deeper band is a legitimate design choice.

finish_group_wording_note: The finish NAMES here are the price page's wording, because that is the page the order is written from. The swatch page (printed p.17) prints some of them in a different word order - 'Pacific Gris Abujardado' there against 'Gris Abujardado Pacific' here - and carries the CE codes. The CE codes are NOT held against these names: matching them would mean deciding that two differently-ordered strings are the same finish, and that is a reading nobody has checked.

ceramic_top.handed_note: A top has no hand. It is cut to the run it covers.
ceramic_top.thickness_note: Thickness is the article's only fixed dimension and it is carried in height_mm, because a top is thin on Z - unlike a sheet panel, which is thin on Y and carries its thickness in depth_mm. Same word, different axis, because they are different objects.
ceramic_top.notes: TWO CODES, ONE PER THICKNESS, and the depth and the finish group are both order axes. The 4 cm is what 545 Avenida Primavera declares: Project.worktop_t_mm is already 40 on that model and the range reservation stands on it (920 = 880 carcass + 40 top), so changing the thickness moves that reservation too.

top_depth_rule.source_ref: CESAR - 3 Linear Elements.pdf printed p.39-40 / PDF 41-42, "Finishes - Modifications" / "Top depths"
top_depth_rule.note: WHAT CESAR RECOMMENDS, PRINTED AS THREE TABLES OF SECTIONS. A top depth is the carcass depth plus a fixed amount PER EXPOSED SIDE, and the amount is the EDGE TREATMENT: standard +30, flush with the door +25, diamond/palmier edge +37. Against a wall only the front is exposed; back to back both are, which is why the double rows add twice. For our 620 carcass with its door face at 644,5: standard = 650, which overhangs the DOOR by 5,5; flush = 645, which overhangs it by nothing.
top_depth_rule.the_eight_bands_are_this_table: EVERY ONE of depth_bands_mm - 380 650 700 750 800 1030 1080 1300 - is a printed STANDARD top depth from this table, all eight, no leftovers on either side. The price page and the planning page are the same list seen twice.
top_depth_rule.a_printed_exception_to_the_closed_list: RECORDED AND NOT IMPLEMENTED. Printed p.40 Notes map every diamond/palmier depth onto the standard band it is priced at - "For 65.7 cm deep tops refer to the price of the 65 cm deep top", and so for all eight. So a 657 top IS orderable and IS priced at band 650, while TopStamp.verify refuses any piece deeper than its band - correctly, on what it knows. Acting on this needs the EDGE PROFILE, an order axis this registry does not hold, so it is a decision and not a patch. The flush depths (375 645 695 745 795 1020 1070 1290) are the mirror case and need nothing: shallower than the band is already allowed, and already remarked on as stone cut down from a wider band.
top_depth_rule.projecting_tops: SEPARATE AND STRICTER, printed p.38. A top that projects BEYOND the cabinets - a breakfast bar - needs feasibility and a quotation FROM CESAR BEFORE THE ORDER IS SENT. Side panels and specific supports are recommended, and the strengthening panel under it must be 10 cm SHORTER than the depth of the projecting part. There is a fixing-hardware line for it at printed p.58. None of the three depth tables covers this case.
